extracted.intended_audience: Congressional staff, policymakers, and DOD/federal procurement officials
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for evaluating and implementing DOD competitive sourcing, public-private (A-76) competitions, FAIR Act inventories, and related procurement/oversight requirements. Focuses on statutory thresholds, required analyses, reporting, protest/challenge procedures, and contract-management quality measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Tender Official (ATO) duties (OMB Circular A-76)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ATO shall (1) be an inherently governmental agency official with decision-making authority; (2) comply with this circular; (3) be independent of the contracting officer (CO), source selection authority (SSA), source selection evaluation board (SSEB), and performance work statement (PWS) team; (4) develop, certify, and represent the agency tender; (5) designate the most efficient organization (MEO) team after public announcement of the standard competition; (6) provide the necessary resources and training to prepare a competitive agency tender; and (7) be a directly interested party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATO must be independent from contracting/selection teams, have decision authority, develop and certify the agency tender, designate the MEO team after announcement, and ensure resources/training are available to prepare a competitive tender.

rubrics_metrics.name: ATO authority to file protests and employee intervention rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Under P.L. 108-375 (Section 326), the agency tender official is granted the authority to serve as an 'interested party' and file a protest on behalf of federal employees unless the ATO determines no reasonable basis for protest. If an interested party files a protest, a person representing a majority of the federal employees engaged in the activities subject to the competition may intervene in the protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATO may initiate protests of A-76 competitions; employee groups representing a majority can intervene. ATO should evaluate reasonableness of protest before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'interested party' for protests
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'interested party' means an actual or prospective bidder or offeror whose direct economic interest would be affected by the award of the contract or by failure to award the contract (31 U.S.C. 3551(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only parties whose direct economic interests are affected qualify to file/participate in bid protests or challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal cost-comparison requirement and savings threshold for conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD must include a formal cost comparison during public-private competitions and conversion to private contractor performance may occur only if there is a cost-savings of '$10 million or 10%' (i.e., contractor costs are at least $10 million or 10% lower than personnel-related cost of the MEO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-private competitions must contain a formal cost-comparison analysis; conversions require meeting the specified dollar or percentage savings threshold versus the MEO personnel-related costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Efficient Organization (MEO) requirement in competitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversions remain in-house unless contractor costs would be at least $10 million or 10 percent lower than the personnel-related cost of the 'Most Efficient Organization.' The ATO must designate the MEO team after public announcement of the standard competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must develop and document an MEO as the baseline for cost comparisons; the MEO's personnel-related cost is the benchmark for any conversion decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for A-76 cost-comparison studies and funding prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory provisions set maximum durations for A-76 studies: prohibitions on funds if a study exceeds specified time limits (examples in statute/appropriations vary: e.g., 24 months for single-function studies; 30 months or 48 months referenced in different provisions for multi-function studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may not use funds to continue A-76 studies that exceed the applicable statutory time limits; timelines differ by statute/appropriation — agencies must track study duration against the correct statutory limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and analysis requirement before contracting out
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain provisions (e.g., Section 8014 and related appropriations provisions) prohibit contracting out activities (particularly those performed by 10 or more civilian employees) unless a 'most efficient and cost-effective analysis' is performed and certified to House and Senate Appropriations Committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before converting activities to contractor performance, agencies must perform a rigorous MEO/cost-effectiveness analysis and certify the results to appropriations committees as required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exemptions to A-76 applicability (wartime/mobilization)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76, Part 7c(3) notes that the Circular and its Supplement are not applicable to DOD in times of a declared war or military mobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During declared war or military mobilization, agencies (DOD) may follow different procurement approaches; A-76 processes are not required to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, tracking, and oversight requirements for contractor workforce
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes require DOD to provide new accountability on reporting the size and scope of the service contractor workforce. The DOD Inspector General must report to Congress (e.g., by Feb 1, 2005) on whether DOD has sufficient employees to conduct competitions and administer contracts and whether DOD has implemented a dependable system to track and assess both cost and quality of functions performed by DOD service contractors. The Secretary of Defense must submit additional reports on policies for contractors supporting deployed forces and on managing contractor personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain reliable tracking systems for numbers/types of contractors, contract value, casualties, legal/disciplinary actions, and be prepared to report to Congress on workforce sufficiency and contractor performance/quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge procedures for FAIR Act inventories (timeline and remedies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies, contractors, and labor unions may file challenges to inclusion/exclusion of activities from agency inventories. Once challenged, agencies must accept the challenge, make changes, or reject it, and must do so within 30 days after the challenge is filed. Aggrieved bidders may also seek legal remedies if not handled expeditiously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must establish prompt procedures to process inventory challenges within 30 days and track appeals and potential legal actions to avoid procurement delays or litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAIR Act inventory submission, publication, and review obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the FAIR Act, OMB will review and consult with agency heads, and the lists (inventories of inherently governmental vs. not inherently governmental functions) will be made available to Congress and the public. The Director of OMB is required to publish the list in the Federal Register 'within a reasonable time thereafter.' Agencies must submit either a compliant inventory or a letter indicating that all FTEs are inherently governmental. Each function should have an associated point of contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must assemble comprehensive inventories, assign points of contact for functions, be prepared for OMB review and public disclosure, and anticipate administrative challenges and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for market research and justification for contract consolidation
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 801 requires the Secretary of Defense and other senior acquisition officials to ensure that any consolidation of contract requirements (contract bundling) provides small businesses with appropriate opportunities; senior acquisition officials must conduct market research, identify alternative contracting approaches, and determine that contract consolidation is necessary and justified before executing an acquisition strategy to consolidate contracts above $5 million.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before consolidating contracts (especially > $5M), conduct documented market research, evaluate alternatives, justify necessity, and ensure small business access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business and subcontracting opportunity protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory provisions (e.g., amendments to 10 U.S.C. 2381 and appropriations language) require that consolidation provide small businesses with appropriate opportunities to serve as prime contractors and subcontractors and protect nonprofit agencies for the blind or severely handicapped by affording them maximum practicable opportunity as subcontractors and suppliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition strategies must include consideration and documentation of small business and qualified non-profit participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full and open competition and applicability to reconstruction contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 805 requires DOD to comply with the Competition in Contracting Act and other procurement laws and regulations for Iraqi reconstruction contracts and to procure contracts through the use of full and open competition. A related provision (Section 1442) requires publication in the Federal Register or Commerce Business Daily of any contracts for repair/maintenance/construction of infrastructure in Iraq that were issued without full and open competition, no later than 30 days after contract entry (with certain temporal limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconstruction contracts are generally to be awarded via full and open competition; non-competitive awards must be publicly disclosed within statutory deadlines and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement restrictions on certain foreign-sourced defense items and waiver process
rubrics_metrics.description: P.L. 108-136 prohibits procurement of certain defense items/components from foreign countries that restrict provision/sale of military goods/services to the United States; the Secretary of Defense must coordinate with the Secretary of State to identify such countries and may exercise waiver authority with written notification and justification to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement officials must consult the DoD/State list of restricted countries and follow waiver/notification procedures when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buy American and specific procurement rule exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions include prohibitions or waivers regarding Buy American requirements: e.g., restrictions on procurement of carbon/alloy/armor steel plate unless melted/rolled in U.S. or Canada; prohibitions exempting fish/shellfish/seafood from Buy American in FY2004; rules on procurement of shipboard anchor and mooring chain (4 inches and under) if not substantially manufactured in U.S.; and waiver of Buy American Act for reciprocal defense procurement agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers must apply statutory Buy American restrictions and note specified exceptions and waiver authorities; documentation must confirm domestic manufacture where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depot maintenance competition exception with full cost comparability
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions permit competitions for depot maintenance activities between DOD and private firms provided the DOD Senior Acquisition Executive certifies that successful bids include comparable estimates of all direct and indirect costs for both public and private bids; policies governing OMB Circular A-76 shall not apply to competitions conducted under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depot maintenance competitions are used, ensure certified, comparable cost estimates across public and private bids and note that alternate competition policies may supersede A-76 in these cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition workforce management and training standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislative proposals (e.g., H.R. 1836 and H.R. 1837) call for statutory changes in management of training, career accession, and career education to improve the federal acquisition workforce, processes, and services; proposals may give the Secretary of Defense authority to implement personnel rule changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should implement structured training, career development, and education programs for acquisition personnel and document workforce improvement plans as required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract award and administration quality standards (GAO-identified deficiencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO and DOD IG audits identified pervasive contract management problems: non-use of prior history to define requirements; inadequate government cost estimates; cursory technical reviews; inadequate competition; failure to award multiple-award contracts where appropriate; inadequate price negotiation memorandums; inadequate contract surveillance; lack of cost control; and absence of performance measures to judge efficiency and effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good contract management requires: using historical data to define requirements; preparing adequate government cost estimates; conducting thorough technical reviews; promoting adequate competition (including multiple-award contracts where suitable); preparing complete price negotiation memoranda; maintaining active surveillance and cost controls; and establishing performance measures for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic competition and savings goal setting
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO concluded that DOD's savings projections did not sufficiently account for the costs of conducting competitions, and that competitions were likely to take longer than projected; establishing realistic competition and savings goals and detailed plans/analyses is key to achieving desired results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must include the costs and timelines of competitions in savings estimates and develop detailed plans/analyses to evaluate practicality and pacing of competitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional reporting and oversight triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes and committee reports require DOD to report to congressional defense committees on progress toward procurement savings goals, to submit various reports by statutory deadlines, and invite congressional oversight hearings on implementation of revised OMB Circulars and competitive sourcing initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement reforms and major competitions should be documented to support required congressional reporting and prepared for oversight hearings.
